To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) the number of significant components is the number of eigenvalues (EV) that are larger than the sum of the mean square error of the data and the mean square error due to noise; (2) this number is estimated by the NSS-stat; (3) this approach is more reliable than the traditional PCA-based methods, and (4) the new method has been implemented in an interactive graphical user-friendly interface.

(i) the number of components in a XANes or EXAFS dataset cannot be estimated accurately by PCA alone; (ii) the number of pure components in a random mixture can be accurately estimated using a new estimator, NSSstat, which includes the s/n ratio of the data in the analysis; (iii) the number of meaningful components in a dataset can be estimated using the scree plot of EVs, but the result may be ambiguous and its accuracy is unknown; and (
the traditional approaches for PCA component-number estimation, i.e., IND, F-test, and the scree plot of EVs, can produce inaccurate and ambiguous results for XANES and possibly EXAFS data.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the number of components in a random mixture of pure compounds can be estimated with a good degree of accuracy using NSS-stat, which is a robust and reliable method that can be used for both XANES and XAFS data.

the NSS-stat is a more accurate and robust estimator than the traditional ones for the number of components in a XANes or EXAFS dataset, and is recommended for use in the analysis of multicomponent systems.
NSS-stat is the best estimator of the number of pure components in a mixture, and the graphical user-friendly interface can be used for a quick analysis of XANES and/or EXAFS datasets.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the number of pure species in a random mixture of XANES data is best estimated by NSS-stat, which provides a reliable estimate of the number of pure components in a random mixture for a given s/n, and is robust to the presence of noise.
the number of components in a multicomponent mixture cannot be reliably estimated by PCA without taking into account the experimental error.
the estimation of the number of pure components in a multicomponent mixture is a challenging task, and the use of a single estimator is not recommended.
